QUIC handshake, stream, keep-alive, and TLS cache tests

# Purpose
This file is a QUIC integration test executable. It creates a server `fd_quic_t` and a client `fd_quic_t` in the same workspace, connects them with `fd_quic_virtual_pair_init`, and drives a full handshake, stream creation, data transfer, connection close, and cleanup sequence. The test uses callbacks such as [`my_connection_new`](<#my_connection_new>), [`my_handshake_complete`](<#my_handshake_complete>), and [`my_stream_rx_cb`](<#my_stream_rx_cb>) to verify that handshake events and stream receive events occur with the expected state and payload data.

The file also checks QUIC state management rules. It validates the TLS handshake cache order and pool usage with [`validate_quic_hs_tls_cache`](<#validate_quic_hs_tls_cache>), tests idle timeout and `keep_alive` behavior, and checks TLS handshake cache eviction and allocation failure behavior against `tls_hs_ttl`. The [`main`](<#main>) function sets up the test environment, creates the QUIC instances with fixed limits, runs service loops to advance protocol state, and then frees all allocated objects before ending with a pass condition.
